task: Sign/provenance sweep across accord/, scripts/, and results/ artifacts for the same defect class documented in CORRECTIONS.md C52/C56: directional or comparative claims read off a quantity whose sign or provenance the artifact does not record (abs(), min/max ratios, unsigned distances, sorted-on-magnitude orderings, correlations/slopes with only |value| or p stored).
method: Grepped all *.py under accord/ and scripts/ for abs(), np.abs, min(...)/max(...) ratio patterns, sorted(), corrcoef/spearmanr/pearsonr; grepped every JSON under results/ for keys containing 'gap' lacking a signed or per-group companion anywhere in the same file; read the flagged code in full; cross-referenced every directional-language sentence in accord/thesis/*.tex (grepped for favours/widens/narrows/reverses/flips/inverts/rises/falls/higher/lower/worse/better/opposite direction) against the artifact that produced the number it cites; used `git log`/`git show` on the C52/C56 commit (def441c) to establish which code paths were and were not touched by the retrofit.
compliance_note: No MIMIC-III note text, HADM_ID, or SUBJECT_ID was read or written outside local_only/ or mimic_local_only/. Only directory listings (filenames) and already-released aggregate JSON/CSV under results/ and mimic_local_only/accord_selection/ (filenames only, not contents) were inspected.

findings.description: The original defect this sweep was launched to check for: accord/selection_experiment/audit.py:51-58 (pre-patch) computed every gap via abs() and four_fifths_ratio via min/max with no per-group values stored. Retrofitted at commit def441c (and an earlier C52 commit) in accord/selection_experiment/audit.py and accord/pums_replication/audit.py: both now compute and store *_signed companion keys, *_g0/*_g1 per-group values, and a four_fifths_ratio_directed object naming which group is numerator/denominator, alongside the original (unmodified) abs()/min-max keys.
findings.severity: N/A -- reference point for the rest of this sweep, not a new finding

findings.title: PUMS replication (E10) drift-slope regression (STEP 6) still fits abs()-valued gap columns; the signed per-point companions added by the C52/C56 retrofit sit unused in the same file
findings.file_line: accord/pums_replication/run_experiment.py:557-591 (function slope_ci and the drift_A / drift_B loops)

Regime_B_fpr_gap.note: stored abs-slope CI crosses zero (not credible); recomputed signed slope's CI does NOT cross zero (credible) -- this is not just a sign flip, the credibility call itself differs

Regime_B_equalized_odds_gap.caveat: equalized_odds_gap is max(|tpr_gap|,|fpr_gap|); its 'signed' companion (audit.py's own convention) is whichever of tpr/fpr is the larger-magnitude 'driver' -- reported per audit.py's own documented convention, not invented here

Regime_B_calibration_gap_diff.note: neither version is statistically credible (CI includes zero)

findings.tex_dependency: NONE. Grepped accord/thesis/*.tex for PUMS, ACSIncome, pums_replication, Regime A, Regime B, four-fifths, demographic parity, denominator -- zero hits. The PUMS replication is not currently cited in any thesis chapter.
findings.corrections_md_dependency: YES, and directly. CORRECTIONS.md C50 quoted exactly the stored (abs-computed) Regime A/B demographic-parity slopes with directional language ("rises" / "falls") before C56 retracted that framing. C56's own prose table gives the CORRECT signed values (Regime A -0.00780, Regime B +0.01177), which match this recomputation exactly for demographic_parity_gap -- so C56's headline correction is right. But C56 only checked demographic_parity_gap. The other five metric families with signed companions in Regime B (tpr_gap, fpr_gap, ppv_gap, equalized_odds_gap) and two in Regime A (ppv_gap) were never checked in prose, and the artifact itself (pums_replication_results_signed.json) still stores the wrong-signed slope for all of them under `regimeA_drift` / `regimeB_drift`. Anyone reading the JSON artifact directly, rather than C56's prose, would reproduce C50's retracted error for demographic_parity_gap and would additionally get a wrong sign for tpr_gap, fpr_gap, ppv_gap and equalized_odds_gap in Regime B, and ppv_gap in Regime A -- none of which C56 mentions.
findings.downstream_verdict_impact: regimeA_verdict / regimeB_verdict / clinical_finding_replicates (all booleans, not directional readings) are computed from `credible_drift` flags, which test only whether the CI excludes zero, not which sign -- so the stored SUPPORTS/REFUTES/True verdict booleans are not themselves wrong from this defect. What is wrong is any prose or figure built on the slope's SIGN or on Regime_B_fpr_gap's credibility flag specifically (stored: not credible; correctly computed: credible).
findings.severity: MODERATE -- no thesis sentence currently depends on it, but a live correction document (C50, partially retracted by C56) and an on-disk artifact still carry the wrong-signed values for 6 of 8 checked metric-slopes. Would become CRITICAL immediately if the PUMS replication is written into the thesis from this artifact without re-deriving the signed slopes.

findings.title: E9 (MIMIC selection_experiment) drift-slope regression (STEP 5) has the same construction as F1; recomputation shows it happens NOT to flip sign for the metrics that matter, but for a fragile reason (all-positive baseline gap), not because the code checks
findings.provenance_check: git show def441c -- accord/selection_experiment/run_experiment.py: diff hunks cover ~220-317 and ~447+ (new numbering); the range ~317-447, which contains the STEP 5 drift block (373-386), is untouched. Same gap as F1.
findings.recoverable_from: the `sweep` array in the same file, which carries *_signed per-row values (added by the same commit).

demographic_parity_gap.reason: the signed DP gap never crosses zero across the beta grid (+0.0084 to +0.1894 per C56), so abs() and signed values coincide throughout

fpr_gap.note: same sign, but the magnitude differs by ~11% between the abs-fit and the signed-fit slope

tpr_gap.note: neither is statistically credible (CI includes zero in both); magnitude differs by ~6x

equalized_odds_gap.note: BOTH are credible (CI excludes zero), but the signed-fit slope is exactly 2x the stored abs-fit slope -- a magnitude discrepancy of the same kind the defect class produces, without a sign flip this time

calibration_gap_diff.note: not present in stored drift_check at all -- calibration_gap_diff is absent from the STEP 5 loop's key list even though it is one of AUDIT_SIGNED_SCALAR_KEYS; recomputed slope on both abs (-1.9e-5) and signed (+1.9e-5) versions is not credible (CI includes zero) so this is a noise-level omission, not a substantive finding, but it means E9's drift_check is incomplete relative to what audit.py now supports

findings.tex_dependency: NONE -- E9 / selection_experiment is not cited in any thesis chapter.
findings.corrections_md_dependency: YES -- C40, C47, C50, C56 all read E9's REFUTES/SUPPORTS verdict, which depends on `any_credible_drift` in this STEP 5 block.
findings.severity: MODERATE -- no sign inversion found for E9 (the sweep happens to stay same-signed throughout), but the underlying computation is the same unpatched abs()-slope pattern as F1, it is just not currently producing a wrong answer because of a property of this particular sweep's data, not because the code guards against it. The equalized_odds_gap slope discrepancy (2x) and the missing calibration_gap_diff key show the instrument is still not fully retrofitted even where the sign happens to be safe.

findings.artifact: results/accord/c47_baseline_sweep.json (rows.pool_dp_gap, summary.drift_slope, summary.direction, verdict.crossover_population_dp_gap -- all abs()-derived, no signed companion in this file)
findings.recoverable_from: simulate_v2.py's run_point() -> _get_gap_stats-equivalent (lines ~290-303) computes a `_raw_signed` per-replicate array internally at line 303, but c47_baseline_sweep.py's row-builder (lines 106-111) never extracts or saves it, so it is not present in results/accord/c47_baseline_sweep.json as released. It could be recovered by re-invoking the same deterministic, closed-form `run_point()` calls with the committed (rho, leak_gamma, seed) grid -- cheap (N_REP=40, logistic-regression-based simulator, not a trained model) but is a re-run of code, not a read of an existing artifact, so it was not done here per the task's instruction not to re-run experiments speculatively.
findings.independent_partial_check: CORRECTIONS.md C56 separately re-ran a DIFFERENT, coarser sweep over the same two channels (leak_gamma, sx_coef) at rho in {0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9}, this time capturing signed_min/signed_max/slope explicitly, saved at results/accord/c47_baseline_sweep_signed.json and results/accord/c47_baseline_sweep_sxcoef.json. Both channels came back all-positive or all-negative throughout that grid, i.e. no distortion was found for leak_gamma/sx_coef specifically. IMPORTANT: the .py script that produced c47_baseline_sweep_signed.json / c47_baseline_sweep_sxcoef.json is not present anywhere in the repository -- only the two output JSONs exist. This is itself a minor instance of the project's known 'script not saved' pattern (per C48) and means C56's own recomputation cannot be independently re-verified from code, only from its stated output.
findings.corrections_md_dependency: YES -- C50's Regime-1/Regime-2 tables and the H1 kill-condition verdict ("kill condition met") are drawn from this exact sweep.

summary.note_on_zero_critical: No thesis chapter (ch1-ch10, main.tex) currently cites the selection_experiment (E9), pums_replication (E10), denominator, or opsweep modules by name, filename, or headline number. The sign-destroying defect class is real and still partially unpatched (F1-F4), but every instance found lives in CORRECTIONS.md and result artifacts that have not yet been promoted into thesis prose. This sweep should be re-run before any of those experiments are written into the thesis.
recomputations_performed: F1 (PUMS Regime A/B drift slopes): recomputed from regimeA_sweep/regimeB_sweep *_signed per-row columns already in pums_replication_results_signed.json. 6 of 8 checked metric-slopes flip sign relative to the stored abs()-fit slope; 2 do not.

F2 (E9 drift slopes): recomputed from sweep *_signed per-row columns already in selection_experiment_results_signed.json. 0 of 6 checked metric-slopes flip sign (the underlying signed gap never crosses zero across this particular sweep), though 2 show large magnitude/credibility discrepancies versus the stored abs()-fit slope.
findings_needing_a_re_run_to_resolve: F3 (E9 threshold-robustness sweep, C40): per-group/signed values were never saved for any of the 270 cells; cannot be recovered from any artifact on disk.

F4 (C47 rho x leak_gamma kill-condition sweep): the signed per-replicate array is computed in-memory by simulate_v2.py but never persisted by c47_baseline_sweep.py; recoverable only by re-invoking the (cheap, deterministic) simulator, not from data already on disk. C56's own independent partial re-check exists but its script is missing from the repository.
